title: Cyrus and the Garden
premise: Xanthe Amberdale, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead in every carved relic, has survived Thornfell's wars by staying neutral — guiding smugglers, carving grave-gifts, trusting no one. When the old gods stir back to life and answer prayers for the first time in three centuries, they mark Xanthe as their messenger and demand a debt: recover the soul of a dead godling sold to the court beneath the mountain by the usurper's priests. Xanthe grudgingly allies with Cyrus, a disgraced temple knight hunting his own stolen memories, and together they descend through smuggler roads and bone-lit courts where justice is bartered rather than written. In the end, Xanthe must choose between loyalty to the living who sheltered them and truth to the dead who made them — paying the price of survival by surrendering their own hearing, going deaf to the dead so the godling's soul can return and the free cities can hold against the usurper's armies.
about_author: Vesper Blackwood is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed remains before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about grief, bargains, and the people who live in the cracks between kingdoms.

chapters.title: The Carver's Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the border town of Hollowmere, Xanthe carves a grave-gift and hears the dead woman's last words: 'They sold her soul.' The emotional beat is wary isolation — Xanthe buries the warning, refusing to get involved, but the voice follows them home.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the shrine of the forgotten god Ashen-Who-Waits, an old woman's prayer is audibly answered for the first time in generations. The town erupts in fear and hope; Xanthe alone hears what the god actually said — a name, and it is theirs.

chapters.title: Cyrus at the Gate
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A disgraced temple knight arrives in Hollowmere hunting rumors of resurrected gods, carrying a broken oath-stone he cannot remember breaking. He interrogates smugglers and finds only one guide willing to take him into Thornfell: Xanthe Amberdale.

chapters.title: The Debt Named
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The god Ashen manifests through carved bone and names its price: its child-godling's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain, and Xanthe will retrieve it or lose the voices forever. The beat is coerced commitment — Xanthe agrees only because silence would be worse.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Xanthe leads Cyrus through the Thornfell passes, testing him with lies and detours. They are ambushed by the usurper's outriders, and Cyrus fights with a skill that frightens both of them — muscle memory from a war he can't recall.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sheltering in a charnel cave, Xanthe reads Cyrus's broken oath-stone and hears fragments of the massacre he was blamed for. The beat is reluctant empathy: the evidence suggests Cyrus was framed, but Xanthe has survived by never believing anyone.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Burn Slow
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Descending toward the lowlands, they find refugee columns fleeing the usurper's advance. Cyrus sees the war he once served now devouring the innocent, and his quest for memory becomes a quest for justice outside any court that would judge him.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Salt
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. To enter the mountain court, Xanthe trades a favor to Mother Quill, a smuggler queen who once saved their life — binding themselves to a future debt. The beat is the cost of old loyalties resurfacing at the worst time.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They pass the threshold into the subterranean court, where the dead serve as currency and lanterns burn on rendered souls. Cyrus's oath-stone begins to warm; something down here recognizes it.

chapters.title: The Court of Rendered Light
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the soul-market, Xanthe locates the godling's soul sealed in a carved reliquary — carved, long ago, in Xanthe's own master's hand. The revelation shatters Xanthe's belief that their teacher died innocent.

chapters.title: Audience with the Usurper's Priest
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. High Priest Vael Corvane, architect of the soul-trade, recognizes Cyrus and offers him his memories back in exchange for betraying Xanthe. The beat is temptation: the truth of his own past, priced against a stranger.

chapters.title: Thief in the Bone Gallery
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The theft of the reliquary goes wrong when the gallery's dead guardians wake. Xanthe must speak with the dead mid-heist, bargaining passage, while Cyrus holds the corridor — and remembers, piece by piece, how to fight like a knight of the old order.

chapters.title: The Master's Confession
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Escaping through service tunnels, Xanthe opens the reliquary's outer case and finds their master's dying confession carved inside: he sold the godling to buy the free cities one generation of peace. Loyalty to the dead teacher collides with the truth of his betrayal.

chapters.title: Mother Quill Collects
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Mother Quill calls in her debt at the worst moment: she wants the reliquary itself, to sell to the highest bidder among the free cities' councils. Xanthe must refuse the person who saved them, choosing the mission over gratitude.

chapters.title: Cyrus Remembers
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cornered by Vael's hunters, Cyrus's full memory returns: he did not commit the massacre — he witnessed it, ordered by the temple, and his superiors erased him. His shame transforms into purpose; he knows exactly where the usurper's armies will strike.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Fleeing the collapsing tunnels, Xanthe realizes the godling's soul can only be freed by a living vessel willing to give up their own gift. Xanthe hides this from Cyrus, planning to pay it secretly — the beat is quiet, terrible resolve.

chapters.title: Armies at the Pass
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Above ground, the usurper's vanguard reaches Thornfell's southern pass. Cyrus rallies scattered refugees and deserters into a holding force at the narrow defile, buying days with knowledge only he possesses.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath Rises
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Vael Corvane pursues them to reclaim the godling, unleashing the court's soul-bound legions. Xanthe chooses to stand and bargain with the dead legionnaires directly, offering them testimony — justice spoken aloud, outside any law.

chapters.title: Judgment of the Dead
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the climactic confrontation, the dead legionnaires turn on Vael after Xanthe speaks their names and crimes aloud. Vael falls; the reliquary opens; and Xanthe steps forward before anyone can stop them, offering their hearing as the vessel-price.

chapters.title: Silence Given
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The godling rises free and whole; the voices of the dead leave Xanthe one by one, each speaking farewell. The beat is grief transfigured — Xanthe chose truth over the survival of the self they were, and does not regret it even while mourning.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Hold
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. With the godling restored, the old gods openly shield the free cities, and the usurper's army breaks at the pass. Cyrus clears his name not through any court but through the testimony of the living and dead alike, and chooses to stay with the refugees rebuilding.

chapters.title: A Carver Who Listens Differently
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Epilogue. Deaf to the dead but not to the living, Xanthe reopens their workshop in Hollowmere, carving grave-gifts that carry no voices — only memory. Cyrus visits with bread and news. The final beat is earned peace: survival was costly, and worth it.
